svg.title: FuncHole synchronous request flow, component wiring, and invocation completion
svg.desc: Animated SVG showing how a client request becomes an invocation, how the dispatcher runs FUNCTION steps through Node artifacts, how the RESPONSE step completes the invocation, and how the terminal JetStream event resolves the Gateway's held HTTP connection with the real response.
svg.text: Gateway holds the HTTP connection open. Dispatcher runs FUNCTION steps through Node artifacts, then RESPONSE completes the invocation and resolves the held response.
Local execution — Node artifact per FUNCTION step

g.text: Calls gateway host, not a function host.
Resolves the adopted Flow and creates the Invocation.
Registers a pending HTTP correlation instead of writing 202.
Never writes to the client connection directly.
Final status + body come from the RESPONSE step's result.
Thread-safe in-memory map, one entry per in-flight request.
Timeout returns 504 and never cancels the Invocation.
Freezes the executable graph for this invocation.
Idempotent conditional UPDATE marks terminal state once.
Publishes only after the DB transition actually happens.
Terminal events carry just the invocationId.
Never assumes position 1 is the first step.
Chooses the next step from the frozen snapshot only.
ACKs JetStream once RUNNING is durably persisted.
Finds compatible runtime capacity for FUNCTION steps only.
Capacity releases only after terminal persistence.
No JetStream on this local hot path.
Does not query Flow or Invocation state.
This is the key component wiring seam.
Runtime maps that version to executable code.
Handler returns output or throws mapped error.
Result travels back over IPC to the Dispatcher.
Executes in the orchestration layer, not on a runtime.
No Runtime Registry reservation, no IPC hop.
A build/execution failure fails the Invocation directly.
Important boundary: NATS + JetStream coordinates globally (ready and terminal); IPC executes locally per FUNCTION step. RESPONSE never touches the Runtime Registry.

The response is truly synchronous: the client connection stays open until INVOCATION_COMPLETED/FAILED resolves the Gateway's pending correlation, or the configurable timeout returns a 504 without cancelling the invocation.
